Fir No. 17/2014

Under Section 354-A/354-D Ipc & 8/12 Pocso Act
State Versus Fareed Ahmed S/o Sh. Aneesh Ahmad,
 R/o B-674/2, Gali No.7, Subhash Vihar,
 North Ghonda, Delhi.

sentences.text:
1. On 04.01.2014, on receipt of DD No.77-B, SI Yogesh Kumar of PS Bhajanpura reached the spot i.e.
a cylinder shop in Gali No. 5, Subhash Mohalla, Bhajanpura, Delhi where he came to know that the complainant and the accused had already been taken to the police station by the PCR officials.

Accordingly, he returned to the PS where the vicitm, a minor girl, aged about 17 years met him and gave a written complaint to him, addressed to the SHO alleging that "she used to go to Shani Bazaar at Ghonda every Saturday to purchase vegetables.
For the last three-four weeks, one boy had been meeting her in the market and used to tease her.
The boy used to ask her to have friendship with him and used to follow her from the market to her house.
She had informed about it to her parents.
Despite her persistent requests, he did not mend his ways.
On 04.01.2014, her brother Neeraj gave her assurance and asked her that she need not fear from that boy and if the boy again repeats his acts, she should inform him on phone.

On that day, at about 07.00pm, when she had gone to market and was purchasing vegetables, the boy again came to her and asked her name and started teasing her and when she started to walk ahead, he caught her hand and teased her.
She then raised an alarm.
Some public persons rescued her from the boy and started beating him.

Meanwhile, she called her brother SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 1 of 10 through phone who came there, caught the boy and made a call at number 100 and a PCR van arrived at the spot.

She came to know the name of the said boy as Fareed Ahmad and also about his parentage and address".
2. On the basis of above complaint, a case was registered for the offences punishable under Section 354(A)(D) IPC and Section 8/12 of the POCSO Act.
The accused was arrested.
The victim was produced before the Ld. MM where her statement under Section 164 CrPC was recorded.
After completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed against accused Fareed Ahmed for the said offences.

1 3.

After hearing arguments on charge and considering the material on record, Ld. Predecessor framed a charge against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 8/12 of the POCSO Act and alternatively under Section 354-A/354-D IPC, dated 24.03.2014, to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
4. In order to establish its case, the prosecution examined ten witnesses at the trial.
5. PW-1 Neeraj Kumar was the brother of the victim, who deposed about the incident.
PW-2 HC Pramod Kumar Tiwari was the duty officer and had recorded the information regarding incident vide DD No.77-B, which he handed over to SI Yogesh Kumar for further proceedings.
6. PW-3 Ct.
Mahesh Kumar was given the custody of the accused by SI Yogesh Kumar at the PS and was also a witness to the arrest proceedings of the accused.
He also got the accused medically examined in the hospital.

7. PW-4 Sh. Ram Tek, Assistant Public Health Inspector, Shahdara, North Zone, EDMC, Delhi produced the birth certificate of the victim and proved it as Ex.PW4/A and deposed that as per the said certificate, the date of birth of the victim was 01.04.1996.
8. PW-5

lady Ct. Snehlata had received the call regarding the incident and proved the PCR form as Ex.PW5/A and a certificate under Section 65-B of the Evidence Act, issued by their nodal officer in respect of the said form, as Ex.PW5/B.
SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 2 of 10 9
. PW-6 ASI Puran Singh had produced the call detail records of PCR van, Baker- 24 and proved it as Ex.PW6/A to Ex.PW6/C, respectively.
PW-7 SI Ajay Pal Singh was the PCR van incharge and had reached the spot on receipt of information from the PCR Headquarter.
10. PW-8 Sh. Israr Babu, alternate Nodal Officer from Vodafone Mobile Services Ltd. proved the call detail records, collected during the course of investigation.
PW- 9 was the victim herself, who deposed about the incident.
PW-10 IO SI Yogesh Kumar deposed about the investigation conducted by him.
11. Statement of the accused was recorded under Section 313 CrPC wherein all the entire incriminating evidence was put to him which he denied and pleaded his innocence.
He took the defence that he was falsely implicated in this case by the victim and her so-called brother with the connivance of the police.

12. In order to prove his innocence, the accused examined one witness in his defence i.e. DW-1 Sh.
Hamid Khan.
13. I have heard Sh. Sukhbeer Singh - Ld. Addl. PP for the State, Sh. Sanjeev Shukla - Ld. Counsel for the accused and have gone through the records.

State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/
2 14.

The main witness of this case was the victim herself whose version was corroborated by PW-1,
her brother.
It is observed that the victim has stood her ground and had maintained her version at every stage of the proceedings.
She made categoric allegations in the FIR which were duly supported by her in her statement under Section 164 CrPC and then in her deposition before the Court.

In her complaint on which the FIR was registered, she alleged that she used to go to purchase vegetables on every Saturday from the weekly market and a boy had been teasing her for the last three-four weeks.
She stated that the said boy used to ask her for having friendship with him and followed her and did not mend his ways.
She further stated that on 01.04.2014, her brother Neeraj gave her courage and also provided his mobile phone and asked her if the said boy again teases, she should call him.

At about 07.00pm, when she was in the market, the said boy came to her, asked SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 3 of 10 her name and started teasing her and when she started to move from there he caught hold of her hand on which she raised an alarm,
hearing which some public persons got her released and gave beatings to the accused.
In the meanwhile, she called her brother who arrived there and called the PCR.
15. The victim gave almost similar statement to the Ld. MM under Section 164 CrPC which is Ex.PW9/B and in her statement before the Court, she made almost identical deposition.
16. She was duly cross-examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel.
However, nothing material came out so as to disbelieve her version.
In other words, her testimony could not be shaken in the cross-examination.
She denied knowing any boy by the name of Gaurav or that said Gaurav was a friend of her brother Neeraj (PW-1).

She admitted that name of her elder uncle (taau) was Sh.
Radhey Shyam but could not say if he had lodged an FIR on 26.03.2013 against Gaurav having kidnapped her.

She was given the suggestion, which was the defence of the accused, that she was recovered alongwith Gaurav at the behest of accused in December, 2013 and thereafter, she and the said Gaurav apprised Neeraj about it and they were annoyed of the acts of the accused and as such,
Neeraj had given beatings to the accused in the market and thereafter, she conspired with Neeraj and implicated the accused in this case.
She denied all these suggestions.
She was also confronted with the copy of the said FIR which she admitted, but submitted further that the final report of the said FIR be also considered.

17. It is worthwhile to mention that the defence so taken by the accused was never proved, that is to say that neither the proceedings of the said FIR or the result of the same was ever placed on record nor the complainant of that case i.e. Sh. Radhey Shyam was never summoned as a witness.

Hence,
this defence, as taken by the accused, was ever proved and mere suggestions would not suffice and would not be sufficient to prove the defence raised by the accused.
The only witness examined by the accused in his defence i.e. DW-1 had deposed that on the day of incident he had seen two persons beating the accused and he intervened.

He further deposed that he SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 4 of 10 heard one of the said boys saying that the accused had informed the family members of the girl and then one of the assailants called the PCR.

This version of this witness does not make out or prove the defence of the accused, but rather corroborates the testimony of the victim that is to say that the accused was beaten by the public persons when she raised alarm on being molested by the accused.

State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/
3 18. DW-1 never disclosed the name of the alleged two boys who were beating the accused and hence,
the defence of the accused that it was Neeraj and Gaurav who had given beatings to the accused,
could not be corroborated and substantiated.

19. Apart from the aforesaid, there was no further cross-examination of the victim and as such, the allegations made by her that the accused used to follow her and had caught her hand twice and particularly on 04.01.2014 in the weekly market when he was beaten by the public, remained unrebutted and unchallenged.

20. The version of the victim was corroborated by PW-1, who deposed that the victim was just like his sister and had informed him through his wife that a boy had been teasing the victim for the last two-three Saturdays when she used to go to the market and used to follow her to her house.
Accordingly he provided his mobile phone to the vicitm on the next Saturday while she was going to the market.

He further deposed that on 04.01.2014 at about 07.00/07.15pm, he received a phone call from the victim on his mobile phone, who disclosed him about the presence of the same boy and further told him that he was teasing her.
Accordingly, he went there and found a crowd and the victim crying and accused was also present there who had been beaten by the public.
Accordingly, he called the PCR.

21. His testimony could also not be shaken in the cross-examination except the fact which he admitted that victim was not his real sister and that she was residing in his house for the last one or two months before the incident.

He also admitted the fact that the uncle of the victim, Sh. Radhey Shyam had lodged a missing report in respect of the victim at PS M.S. Park on 26.03.2013 but denied the suggestion that the victim had married with one Gaurav.

He was confronted with his previous SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 5 of 10 statement Ex.PW1/BA wherein he had not stated that the victim had told his wife that accused used to tease her.

Again there was no cross-examination of this witness on the material aspects that is to say that when this witness deposed that the victim had apprised him about the accused teasing her and following her or that on 04.01.2014, the victim called him on mobile phone again apprising him of the accused molesting her and his reaching the place and his having found the accused being beaten by the public and the victim found crying by him.
In this way, PW-1 has corroborated the testimony of PW-9 in material particulars and there was no cross-examination of either of the two witnesses.

22. PW-7 was the incharge of the PCR van, who reached the spot and he too deposed that on reaching the spot, he found many public persons apart from the victim and her brother Neeraj, who produced the accused before him with allegations that he had molested the victim.
He then took all of them to PS Bhajanpura by his PCR van.
He identified the accused in the Court.

In his cross- examination though he admitted that the incident of molestation had not taken place in his presence, however, he also deposed that the public persons, victim and her brother informed him about the molestation committed by the accused.
Counsel for the accused argued that initially information given to the PCR was regarding a quarrel as deposed by PWs 6 and 7, which raises suspicion about the allegations.

I differ with this argument as it was not incorrect since the accused was beaten by the public persons and in the State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/
4 mellee any one could have been confused it with a quarrel.

entities.text: State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, it was argued that Neeraj was not the real brother of the victim.
Again this has no relevance with the incident or the nature of allegations.
As already observed, hereinabove, the defence raised by the accused could not be proved.
It was also submitted by the Ld. Counsel that as per the testimony of PW-10, the IO public persons were present at the spot.
He submitted that despite that the IO never made any inquiries from them nor cited them as witnesses in this case.

Again this argument is bereft of any merits as public persons hardly come to become witnesses in a case now-a-days and the value attached to the SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 6 of 10 testimony of the victim which could not be shaken in the cross-examination, would not diminish because of the non joining of the public witnesses.
24. It is thus clearly seen that both PW-1 and PW-9 stood their ground and their testimony could not be shaken in the cross-examination.

It has been duly proved and established by PW-2 and PW-9 (the victim) that the accused used to follow her and pester her for friendship and on two occasions,
particularly on 01.04.2014 at a public place, the accused had also caught hold of her hand.

This act of the accused should have been with sexual intent as there is a presumption as regard the mental status of the accused under Section 30(1) of the POCSO Act as under:
"Presumption of culpable mental state - (1) In any prosecution for any offence under this Act which requires a culpable mental state on the part of the accused, the Special Court shall presume the existence of such mental state but it shall be a defence for the accused to prove the fact that he had no such mental state with respect to the act charged as an offence in that prosecution"
25.
In view thereof, it is held that the prosecution has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The accused was charged for the offences under Section 12 and 8 of the POCSO Act and alternatively under Section 354-A IPC and 354-D IPC.

However, Section 42 of the POCSO Act provides that "wherein an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under any other law for the time being in force then, notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment only under such law or this Act as provides for punishment which is greater in degree".
Accordingly, accused Fareed Ahmed is held guilty for the offences punishable under Sections 12 and 8 of the POCSO Act and is convicted as such.
Put up for arguments/order on the quantum of sentence as per the schedule given in the ordersheet.
PRONOUNCED IN OPEN COURT ON 20th day of December 2016 (Sanjay Sharma-I) Addl.

5 1.
Vide judgment dated 20.12.2016, convict Fareed Ahmed was held guilty and convicted for the offences punishable under Section 8/12 POCSO Act.

2. I have heard Sh. Sukhbeer Singh -Ld. Addl. PP for the State, assisted by Ms.
Shabnam Khan - Advocate/RCC Lawyer and Sh. Sanjeev Shukla - Ld. Counsel for the convict.
3. It was submitted by the Ld. Addl. PP that maximum punishment should be awarded to the convict since he has been found guilty of molesting and teasing the victim, a minor girl, aged about 17 years.
4. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the convict submitted that the convict is aged about 26 years.
It was further submitted that he is unmarried and is working in DTC as a conductor on daily wages and that he has to look after his aged parents, younger brother and a younger marriageable sister.
It was further submitted that the convict is a first time offender with no criminal antecedents nor is wanted in any other case of criminal nature.
5. An application had also been moved under Section 3 and 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act read with Section 360 CrPC with a prayer to release him on probation of good conduct.
SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 8 of 10 6.
I have considered the mitigating and the aggravating circumstances as presented before me.
The convict has already remained in JC for a period of two months during the trial.

7. In Daulat Ram Vs. State of Haryana AIR 1972 SC 2434, it was observed that Section 6 of Probation of Offender Act should be liberally construed so that its operation may be effective and beneficial to the young offenders who are prone more easily to be led astray by the influence of bad company.

entities.text: Daulat Ram Vs. State of Haryana AIR 1972 SC 2434
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further observed that their stay in jail might well attract them towards a life of crime instead of reforming them.

It is for this reason that the mandatory injunction against the imposition of sentence of imprisonment has been embodied in Section 6.
8.
It is a matter of record that the prosecution has failed to place on record any previous history of conviction or even involvement of the convict in other criminal acts.
The age of the convict is also not in dispute.
The incident proved against the convict is trivial in nature and not very uncommon in the present day youth.
9. It was argued by the Ld. Addl. PP that since minimum sentence has been provided in Section 8 of the POCSO Act, therefore, the convict cannot be released on probation.
I disagree with this contention.
Section 8 of the POCSO Act or any other provision of this Act regarding awarding of sentence do not have any overriding effect upon the Probation of Offenders Act.
There are various other enactments which provide for minimum sentence yet the courts have adverted to the provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act.

In Ishar Dass Vs. State of Punjab 1972 AIR 1295 SC,
the appellant was convicted for the offence under Section 7 (1) of the Prevention of Food State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/
6 Adulteration Act which carries a minimum sentence of imprisonment of six months, yet the the benefit of Probation SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 9 of 10 of Offenders Act was extended to him.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the contention of the Ld. Addl. PP cannot be accepted.
10.In my opinion a chance should be given to the convict considering his age and family backgrounds.

Accordingly, the plea of the convict is accepted and he is directed to be released on probation of good conduct for a period of two years on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.25000/- with one surety in the like amount, with direction that in case of any default he shall be called upon to receive the sentence.
He is directed to keep peace and be of good behaviour during this period.
11.A probationary officer shall be appointed who shall keep vigil upon the convict and his activities.

The convict shall apprise his latest residential address to the probationary officer and shall not leave Delhi without his permission and shall also not change his address without prior intimation to him.
12.A copy of this order be sent to the Probationary Officer attached to the Court who shall furnish his report regarding the conduct and behaviour of the convict after every 6 months to this Court.
A copy of the judgment and the order on sentence be given free of cost to convict.

Accordingly, the plea of the convict is accepted and he is directed to be released on probation of good conduct for a period of two years on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.25000/- with one surety in the like amount, with direction that in case of any default he shall be called upon to receive the sentence.
He is directed to keep peace and be of good behaviour during this period.
